speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and have you noticed any recent injuries or insect bites in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a pop or feel a sudden loss of strength in the finger, and are you currently unable to fully straighten the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of the inability to flex the fingertip after a forceful extension injury, this sounds like a classic "Jersey Finger" injury involving the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I am going to order an X-ray to rule out an avulsion fracture at the tendon's attachment point. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the X-ray is negative for fracture, the injury is likely a pure tendon avulsion. To confirm the extent of the injury, I need to visualize the tendon's position. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative X-ray confirms this is a soft tissue injury, specifically a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion. Can you tell me if you can actively flex the distal joint when you hold the middle joint in extension?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
